title: What a Logarithm Is
short: log_b(x) is the exponent you put on b to get x.
trouble: Students read log₂ 8 as 2 · 8 or as 8/2.

blocks.html: To solve $2^x = 8$ you ask, "2 to what power is 8?" A logarithm is the name for that answer. It is the inverse of the exponential function.
$\log_b x$ is the exponent you put on $b$ to get $x$: $\log_b x = y$ means $b^y = x$ (with $b > 0$, $b \ne 1$, $x > 0$). Special names: $\log x$ means $\log_{10} x$ and $\ln x$ means $\log_e x$.

Because $b^x$ is one-to-one, every positive number is $b$ to exactly one power. So "the exponent that gives $x$" is well defined, and that defines a function. A logarithm is an exponent: $\log_2 8 = 3$ because $2^3 = 8$. Logs count how many factors of $b$ make $x$, including fractional and negative counts: $\log_2 \frac{1}{8} = -3$ and $\log_4 2 = \frac{1}{2}$.

blocks.name: logscale
blocks.cap: A linear number line and a logarithmic one. On the log line, equal steps are equal factors: 1, 10, 100 and 1000 are evenly spaced, because their logs are 0, 1, 2, 3.

blocks.html: Reading $\log_2 8$ as $2 \cdot 8$ or $8 \div 2$. A log is not multiplication or division; it answers "what exponent?" Check by raising the base to your answer: $2^3 = 8$, so $\log_2 8 = 3$.
